questions.q: In the "cards, conversations, confirmation" model, what do conversations provide?
choices: The detail a short card can't hold on its own
questions.explanation: A card (user story) is just a short placeholder — a reminder to have a conversation. The conversation fills in the edge cases, constraints, and context the card couldn't hold. Confirmation (acceptance criteria) then nails down what 'done' actually means.

choices: In the browser (and, as covered later, on servers too)
questions.explanation: JavaScript was originally browser-only, but today it also runs on servers via Node.js (covered in Lesson 7). That's what 'full stack JavaScript' means — one language front to back.

questions.q: Which habit most directly prevents a project from becoming unmaintainable later?
choices: Writing documentation as you go, not reconstructing it later
Waiting until the end to plan
questions.explanation: Documentation reconstructed from memory is always incomplete. Writing it as you go captures decisions while they're fresh and prevents future-you (or a teammate) from having to reverse-engineer why something was built the way it was.
